prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: A very small quick hand reaching out of an open drawer in the little spirit's body and snatching a pencil from behind his ear; the spirit squealing; the Vetāla amused; Dādī and Śuka laughing; firelight.
Character appearances:
you: Always seen from behind or at a distance, face never detailed, so every learner can be the hero: a young person in a simple ochre kurta with a cloth shoulder bag.
dadi: A warm, sharp-eyed grandmother in her seventies, silver hair in a low bun, round spectacles, a cream cotton sari with a thin maroon border and a grey shawl; carries a cloth-bound notebook.
shuka: A bright green rose-ringed parrot with a red beak and a faint pink and black neck ring, a little scruffy, very expressive eyes; usually on your shoulder or Dādī's.
vetala: A long, thin, ash-grey spirit hanging upside down from a śiṃśapā branch by its ankles, arms folded across its chest, bright amused eyes, a shawl of mist trailing downwards; strange, never frightening.
dhatuka: A small, round, honey-brown spirit with ten tiny brass-handled drawers set into his body, a pencil behind one ear, forever hurrying.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
Writing is permitted by the owner. This particular scene needs no readable inscription; focus on its narrative. Do not invent scripts or fill small objects with pseudo-lettering. No watermark or UI.
Put the approved roots and corresponding forms in a clear, short ledger list, one root/form pair per row. No additional writing. All human and humanoid figures wear complete opaque traditional clothing or robes.
